summary: linux-fleet-compat gets its own skip-policy entry and lane (shadow, enforce false) keyed by what the fleet-compat stage reads: crate fractal's dependency closure and its #[path] includes, the toolchain, the fleet baseline and the scripts the stage runs; its gate job runs beside linux-gate's, and its own run checks the stage's compile reads against the key (scripts/dep-info-check, warnings in shadow)

replay.detail: No record, signature or storage format changes; CI's fleet-compat stage note is keyed by the new entry's inputs.

schema.detail: No schema change: the entry uses the policy's existing keys.

rules.detail: Shadow only: the linux-fleet-compat gate never says skip while enforce is false, and linux-gate still covers fleet-compat as before.

compatibility.detail: Existing notes and checks are unchanged. scripts/st-test --all is unchanged; --check linux-fleet-compat signs the stage on request.

recovery.detail: Revert the change; the shadow entry, lane and gate job go with it.
